A_occupant_distribution.current_range: 3 templates used (10/10/10/10, 5/5/15/15); the robust-generalization audit also used 12/8/12/8, 16/4/16/4, 4/16/4/16
A_occupant_distribution.physically_meaningful: any non-negative split of 40 across the four rooms
A_occupant_distribution.useful_diversity: HIGH: the only dimension that changes tick-0 inputs
A_occupant_distribution.confounding: occupant ids are assigned R1-first and baseline exits are id-parity based, so mirror-image templates are not exactly symmetric; disclosed, not a leak

B_compliance_probability.changes_observable_state: only indirectly and only after hub admissions (corridor counts); never at t=0
B_compliance_probability.useful_diversity: HIGH for outcomes, LOW for inputs
B_compliance_probability.confounding: With one key and one seed, the p=0.5 compliant set is a subset of the p=0.9 set and the vector is identical across every t_h. Reusing a (key, seed) across a training cell and a test cell would give nearly the same hidden compliance on both sides of the split. Keys must include the split role and seed ranges must be disjoint by role.

C_hazard_onset.physically_meaningful: 3..10 or none; onsets after about tick 13 fall after evacuation ends and are equivalent to none
C_hazard_onset.changes_observable_state: only after onset (residual capacity), never before
C_hazard_onset.useful_diversity: HIGH for outcomes; post-onset inputs only
C_hazard_onset.confounding: must be crossed with distribution and p (full factorial), never tied to a template

D_hazard_location.reason: topology.cap_h_ce1/edge_capacity hard-code H_CE1; varying it requires a simulator change (forbidden). Fixed and disclosed.

E_initial_congestion.reason: reset places occupants only in R1..R4
indirect_sources: epsilon-perturbed pre-decision history (epsilon=0.5, a uniformly random GLOBAL action at each pre-decision tick)

F_behavioral_parameters.reason: no other behavior parameter exists without a simulator change

G_other.reason: module constants; changing them changes the simulator model

compliance_vector_behavior.consequence: With one key and one seed, the p=0.5 compliant set is a subset of the p=0.9 set and the vector is identical across every t_h. Reusing a (key, seed) across a training cell and a test cell would give nearly the same hidden compliance on both sides of the split. Keys must include the split role and seed ranges must be disjoint by role.
